status_summary: On 2025-02-01 Executive Order 14193 imposed duties on Canadian goods with energy resources at 10 percent rather than 25 percent, a measure that cut against free energy flow, and Executive Order 14389 of 2026-02-20 ended those IEEPA duties. The National Security Strategy released 2025-12-04 calls for building resilient energy infrastructure with regional partners. Executive Order 14373 of 2026-01-09 and OFAC General License 46 of 2026-01-29 opened Venezuelan oil to trade by established US companies under conditions, and on 2026-04-30 a Presidential Permit authorized Bridger Pipeline Expansion LLC to build a 36-inch crude oil border pipeline in Phillips County, Montana.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14193 imposed additional duties on Canadian imports, with qualifying energy resources subject to a 10 percent rate rather than 25 percent.
The White House released the National Security Strategy (dated November 2025), which calls for scalable and resilient energy infrastructure with Western Hemisphere partners.
Executive Order 14373 placed Venezuelan government oil revenue funds in US custody as sovereign property, with the Secretary of Energy consulted on their management.
OFAC issued General License 46 authorizing established US companies to engage in Venezuelan-origin oil trade under conditions.
Executive Order 14389 ended the additional IEEPA duties imposed under nine earlier orders, including EO 14193 on Canadian goods.
A Presidential Permit authorized Bridger Pipeline Expansion LLC to construct and operate a 36-inch crude oil pipeline crossing the US-Canada border in Phillips County, Montana.

title: Hemisphere-focused energy policy with Mexico, Canada and others to raise production
uncertainties: Executive Order 14389 ended the EO 14193 duties, but any remaining non-IEEPA tariffs on Canadian energy (for example under section 232) were not checked. Mexico energy policy, LNG export approvals and Canadian electricity were not researched. The Keystone XL link comes from trade press; the permit itself names only Bridger Pipeline Expansion LLC. The blocker on Canada talks and the USMCA review status rest on a law firm alert. Whether Venezuelan oil licensing is a hemisphere-focused energy policy in the Mandate's sense is a judgment call.
